# Photo dark-mode fixtures

`mixed.pdf` is a deterministic, hand-authored PDF object graph generated by
`tool/generate_photo_fixture.py`. It contains native text, vector paths, a
photograph, a raster plot, a screenshot, a smooth gradient, grayscale imagery,
a large scan-like raster, overlapping text, a clipped image, an alpha image,
a Form XObject, a skewed image, and a native highlight annotation. Its pages
cover all four quarter-turn rotations and nonzero crop/media origins.
`manifest.json` records page expectations and the PDF SHA-256.

`astronaut.png` is a 256 × 256 RGB Lanczos reduction of the 512 × 512 NASA
photograph of Eileen Collins distributed by scikit-image v0.25.2:

- [Source image](https://github.com/scikit-image/scikit-image/blob/v0.25.2/skimage/data/astronaut.png)
- [Source description and public-domain statement](https://github.com/scikit-image/scikit-image/blob/v0.25.2/skimage/data/_fetchers.py#L382)

The source describes the NASA image as public domain with no known copyright
restrictions. The photograph is test data; no endorsement is implied.
All other figure graphics are generated by the fixture script. No external
PDFs, personal documents, or runtime downloads are needed for these fixtures.

The five `.rgb` files are 64 × 64 × 3 center-sampled RGB bytes, without headers.
They match the native sampler and permit classifier tests without a decoder.
The gray photograph is deliberately rejected by this first classifier.

Regenerate from the app directory with Python 3 and Pillow (tested with 12.3.0):

```sh
python3 tool/generate_photo_fixture.py
```

The committed PDF and samples are the test inputs. Regeneration can vary with
Pillow's font rasterizer across versions; compare the manifest/hash before
accepting changes. The photograph itself is already resized and committed.
